bib.title: Imagine while Reasoning in Space: Multimodal Visualization-of-Thought

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Imagine while Reasoning in Space: Multimodal Visualization-of-Thought" (MVoT). Chengzu Li, Wenshan Wu, Huanyu Zhang, Yan Xia, Shaoguang Mao, Li Dong, Ivan Vulic, Furu Wei (Microsoft Research / Cambridge / CAS). arXiv:2501.07542v1, 13 Jan 2025. Preprint (the PDF shows no venue).

COVERAGE: All 27 of 27 pages, 81,991 of 81,991 chars. This covers the main text, limitation, references (skimmed), appendices A-D, tables 1-16 and the figure text. Figures were not rendered, and I did not run the captions script. Figure content comes from the extracted text only.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: MVoT (the model writes an image after each verbal reasoning step, then conditions on it) is the paper's method. It reaches 92.95%, 95.14% and 85.60% on Maze, MiniBehavior and FrozenLake. It is the only fine-tuned variant that beats Direct on all three tasks.
  number: 0.9295 / 0.9514 / 0.8560
  setup: Anole-7B (built on Chameleon-7B), LoRA, 40 epochs, trained on the authors' own grid datasets. Metric is multiple-choice accuracy on held-out test sets of 1255, 1604 and 1664 items.
  quote: "MV oT demonstrates comparable performance on MAZE (92.95%) and MINI BEHAVIOR (95.14%), while achieving a higher accuracy of 85.60% on FROZEN LAKE compared to both Direct and CoT."
  where: p.6; Table 2, p.7
- claim: Text CoT does better than MVoT on the two easy tasks but collapses on FrozenLake, which has more entities and more visual detail.
  number: CoT 0.9792 / 0.9812 / 0.6148 versus Direct 0.7788 on FrozenLake
  setup: CoT is fine-tuned to write textual coordinates AND the environment layout. Same Anole-7B setup.
  quote: "CoT achieves over 95% accuracy on the MAZE and MINI BEHAVIOR by explicitly describing the environment layout and agent location with textual coordinates. However, it performs worse than the Direct baseline on FROZEN LAKE."
  where: p.6; Table 2
- claim: Most CoT errors on FrozenLake come from wrong textual coordinates for the holes. CoT accuracy falls as the grid grows, while MVoT stays flat.
  number: 90.80%; CoT 0.9401 at 3x3 down to 0.3911 at 6x6; MVoT 0.8623 / 0.8397 / 0.8377 / 0.8876 across sizes 3-6
  setup: FrozenLake, grid sizes 3-6. Hole counts rise from about 4.7 to 9.6 as the grid grows (Table 7).
  quote: "Error analysis reveals that 90.80% of CoT's mistakes on FROZEN LAKE stem from inaccurate coordinate descriptions of holes in the environment."
  where: p.6; Tables 7 and 15, pp.17 and 24
- claim: CoT needs the textual layout caption. If it only tracks the agent coordinates, it falls below Direct on all three tasks.
  number: CoT without layout 0.7023 / 0.6000 / 0.5974, against Direct 0.7171 / 0.7250 / 0.7788
  setup: Anole-7B, same tasks.
  quote: "- w/o layout ✓ ✗ ✗ Text 0.7023 ↓ 0.6000 ↓ 0.5974 ↓"
  where: Table 2, p.7
- claim: Token discrepancy loss L_D improves visualization quality and final accuracy. L_D is the sum over image tokens of the embedding-space distance (MSE between visual codebook embeddings) from the label token, weighted by the predicted probability. Total loss is L = L_C + L_D.
  number: Maze accuracy 0.9295 with L_D versus 0.7468 without. MiniBehavior accuracy 0.9514 versus 0.7228. FrozenLake accuracy 0.8560 versus 0.7260. Maze V-Acc 0.9339 versus 0.6391. Maze V-Red 0.1010 versus 0.4931.
  setup: MVoT recursive generation, Anole-7B. The visualization metrics were measured only for Maze and MiniBehavior because FrozenLake is hard to score automatically.
  quote: "We also witness a performance drop on FROZEN LAKE without token discrepancy loss from 0.8560 to 0.7260."
  where: p.9; Table 3, p.9; Table 16
- claim: Training on interleaved image-text data helps even when the loss ignores the image tokens. It still hurts on FrozenLake.
  number: Interleaved 0.8678 / 0.8406 / 0.6460, which is over 10 points above Direct on Maze and MiniBehavior and below Direct on FrozenLake.
  setup: Interleaved computes the loss on text tokens only. MVoT computes it on all tokens.
  quote: "the inclusion of interleaved visualizations during training, despite not contributing directly to the loss, improves performance on MAZE and MINI BEHAVIOR by over 10%."
  where: p.7
- claim: MVoT can act as a plug-in for GPT-4o. The visual thoughts come from the fine-tuned MVoT model and are handed to GPT-4o after it writes its verbal step.
  number: GPT-4o zero-shot Direct 0.7100 / 0.4576 / 0.4976; zero-shot CoT 0.7386 / 0.4676 / 0.4664; with visual thought 0.8556 / 0.6440 / 0.8021
  setup: GPT-4o 2024-07-01 on Azure, temperature 0. Visual thoughts are generated by Anole-7B MVoT.
  quote: "We witness an improvement in performance by over 15% accuracy across all the tasks as shown in Table 2."
  where: p.8; Table 2
- claim: MVoT and CoT fail on different items. Taking the better of the two on each item gives an upper bound near 100% on Maze and MiniBehavior and 92% on FrozenLake.
  number: 0.9984 / 1.0000 / 0.9246
  setup: Per-item oracle union of the two fine-tuned models' predictions. It is not an achievable system.
  quote: "the upper-bound performance reaches nearly 100% accuracy on Maze and MINI BEHAVIOR, and 92% accuracy on FROZEN LAKE."
  where: p.9; Table 4
- claim: The text-token embeddings and the image-codebook embeddings in autoregressive MLLMs are poorly aligned. This is the stated reason for L_D.
  number: about 1 of the top-10 and about 20% of the top-50 similar tokens overlap
  setup: Chameleon, LVM and LlamaGen embeddings, compared by cosine-similarity top-k overlap (Figure 6).
  quote: "on average, only one token overlaps among the top 10 similar tokens, and approximately 20% of tokens overlap among the top 50 similar tokens."
  where: p.10
- claim: With L_D, about 95% of consecutive visualizations are correct during recursive generation.
  number: "95%" (Maze V-Ratio 0.9449, MiniBehavior 0.9618)
  setup: Maze and MiniBehavior only.
  quote: "MV oT withLD achieves an average of 95% correct and consecutive visualizations during reasoning."
  where: p.9
- claim: Headline abstract claim: MVoT beats CoT "by over 20%" in the hard setting. This refers to FrozenLake (0.8560 vs 0.6148, about 24 points).
  number: over 20%
  setup: FrozenLake only. CoT is ahead on the other two tasks.
  quote: "outperforming traditional CoT by over 20% in challenging scenarios."
  where: p.3

Training and data details
- Training data is interleaved text and image targets. During training the next image is conditioned on the golden previous image ("image editing"). At inference it is conditioned on the model's own generated images (recursive).
- Input augmentation: tokenize and detokenize the input image a random 0-10 times to reduce error from image reconstruction (p.18).
- Datasets (Table 1): Maze has 5007 train and 1255 test, grid 3-6, 9.11 actions on average. MiniBehavior has 6400 train and 1604 test, grid 5-8 in Table 1 but 7-10 in the appendix (Table 6), 7 action types. FrozenLake has 6846 train and 1664 test, grid 3-6, 3 answer choices.
- Hyperparameters (Table 8): LR 2e-4, 40 epochs, seed 42. 8 GPUs for Direct and CoT, 32 GPUs for Interleaved and MVoT, all on MI300X.

LIMITS
- Authors concede (Limitation section): "the generated visualizations often attempt to reconstruct task-irrelevant details, such as the background patterns in FROZEN LAKE, while overlooking the intended alterations". Their suggested fix is guidance techniques from diffusion (Sadat et al. 2024).
- Authors concede: "explicitly generating visualizations introduces computational overhead during inference". They suggest compact image representations with fewer tokens. The paper reports no latency or token cost.
- Image detail blurs as patterns get more complex. Tokenize/detokenize reconstruction itself loses fine detail.
- Only three synthetic grid worlds, one 7B backbone, a single seed (42), and no confidence intervals. The datasets are the authors' own, and the MiniBehavior grid-size range is stated inconsistently (Table 1 vs Table 6/Appendix B).
- The FrozenLake visualization metrics were not computed. The robustness claim for FrozenLake therefore rests on task accuracy alone.
- The baselines are weak or biased in places. CoT is given hand-built textual layout captions. GPT-4o is zero-shot and not fine-tuned, so GPT-4o versus Anole is not like-for-like. The GPT-4o+MVoT result is a plug-in with the fine-tuned Anole as the visual generator.
- CoT beats MVoT on Maze (0.9792 vs 0.9295) and MiniBehavior (0.9812 vs 0.9514). Only FrozenLake favours MVoT, and "robust" is the authors' framing.
- The "Direct" baseline overfits (about 70%).
- Dated: the models are Chameleon/Anole, early-fusion discrete-token autoregressive models. The paper names Gemini 2, Transfusion and LatentLM as native generators. It says MVoT could extend to other architectures, but this was not tested.

BUILDS ON
- Visualization-of-Thought (VoT), Wu et al. 2024 (the same lead author), which used textual "visualizations". Chain-of-Thought, Wei et al. 2022.
- Chameleon (Chameleon Team 2024) and Anole (Chern et al. 2024) as the backbone. Image tokenizer from Esser, Rombach and Ommer 2021 (Taming Transformers).
- ReAct (Yao et al. 2023), MM-ReAct (Yang et al. 2023) and Visual Sketchpad (Hu et al. 2024), which are the tool-based visual-thought baselines it argues against.
- Tasks and datasets: maze-dataset (Ivanitskiy et al. 2023), Mini-BEHAVIOR (Jin et al. 2023), FrozenLake via Gym (Brockman 2016) and VSP (Wu et al. 2024, WZS+24).
- Motivation: SAT (Ray et al. 2024), TopViewRS (Li et al. 2024), dual-coding theory (Paivio 1991), working memory (Baddeley 1992).
- LoRA (Hu et al. 2021). L_D relates to JetFormer (Tschannen et al. 2024), which noted similar embedding-alignment limits.

CODE: No code is given in the paper. The core formulas are:
- Eq. 4: L_D = sum over i=1..n of S_{t_vis_i} · P(t_i), where S is the MSE distance row in the visual embedding space.
- Eq. 5: L = L_C + L_D.
- Eq. 1-2: v_i ~ P(v_i | z_1, v_1, ..., v_{i-1}, z_i); z_{i+1} ~ P(z_{i+1} | x, z_1, v_1, ..., z_i, v_i).
- The GPT-4o+MVoT prompt template is in Table 14, p.23. The model simulates one action per turn as "Reasoning i / Action i", waits for the "Observation i: <VISUALIZATION>", and ends with "The answer is X".

FIGURES (captions only, not viewed)
- Fig 1 (p.1): Direct vs CoT vs MVoT interleaved text and image reasoning. This is the quickest overview.
- Fig 2 (p.3): worked MVoT traces for Maze, MiniBehavior and FrozenLake.
- Fig 3 (p.4): training diagram of token discrepancy loss L_D.
- Fig 4 (p.8): FrozenLake visualizations with vs without L_D, and reconstruction blur.
- Fig 5 (p.9): V-Acc and V-Red over training steps on Maze, with and without L_D.
- Fig 6 (p.10): top-k embedding overlap for Chameleon, LVM and LlamaGen.
- Figs 7-8 (pp.25-26): Maze and MiniBehavior visualization failures with and without L_D.
- Fig 9 (p.26): image reconstruction after 10 tokenize/detokenize rounds.
- Fig 10 (p.27): a case where CoT gives wrong hole coordinates and MVoT gets the right answer.

PROBLEMS: Extraction was clean, apart from "MV oT" spacing and some figure text mixed into the body. No embedded instructions were found in the PDF. In Table 2 the "Interleaved" row shows "Image ✓", and the GPT-4o "With Visual Thought" row carries a footnote. Table 5 is labelled Dev, while Table 1 calls the same split Test (same sizes). The Table 15 MiniBehavior CoT overall is 0.9813, against 0.9812 in Table 2 (a rounding difference).
